clues: This small town in Massachusetts sits southwest of Boston. Its old mills made cloth when mills were new in the United States.
Snow can fall here from late fall to spring, in a cold continental climate. The top heat on record was 104 degrees, and the low was far below zero.
In 1727, this place split off to form its own town. It was named for an earl, a lord with a grand old title.
A woman here, Lydia Taft, is claimed as the first woman voter in the colonies. The state also had its first women jurors right here in this town.
A blue cloth made in this town was used for the first dress uniform of the United States Air Force. That bright blue was named for the town itself.
